problem: Which of the following functions is continuous on the interval $(-\infty ,-1]?$  You may assume that all points of discontinuity for each function are shown.
worked_solution:
The correct answer is the following.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945275/assets/7225a16c8dfa80bc750607b30c6deb30bb82807365c0c975c6b5ae3e33e11c6f.png)

We see that $h(x)$ is continuous on the interval $(-\infty ,0],$ and since $(-\infty ,-1]$ lies completely inside $(-\infty ,0],$ it is also continuous on $(-\infty ,-1].$

Notice that:

- $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are not continuous at $x=-2$, and so are not continuous on $(-\infty ,-1].$

- $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ are not continuous at $x=-3$, and so are not continuous on $(-\infty ,-1].$
